title: n & (n − 1): drop the lowest set bit

steps.caption: 44 in binary is 101100. Count the 1-bits. Trick: n & (n − 1) clears the LOWEST 1-bit.
n − 1 flips the lowest 1-bit to 0 and every 0 below it to 1.
AND them: the lowest 1-bit is gone, everything above it is unchanged. count = 1.

n is 0 after 3 steps: exactly one loop per set bit. n & (n − 1) == 0 also tests "is n a power of two?".
